Differentiate between Parallels of Latitude and Meridians of Longitude.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Parallels of Latitude are full horizontal circles parallel to the Equator that decrease in size towards the poles. 2. Meridians of Longitude are equal-length vertical semi-circles running from North to South Pole. 3. Latitudes range from 0° to 90° N/S, while Longitudes range from 0° to 180° E/W.

questions.question_text: Calculate the time difference between Greenwich (0°) and a place located at 30° East longitude.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Earth rotates 1° in 4 minutes (15° per hour). 2. Time difference for 30° = 30 × 4 = 120 minutes = 2 hours. 3. Since the place is East of Greenwich, time is ahead: Greenwich time + 2 hours.

questions.question_text: Explain the three main heat zones of the Earth with neat descriptions of their climatic conditions.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Torrid Zone: Lies between Tropic of Cancer (23.5°N) and Tropic of Capricorn (23.5°S). Receives direct vertical sunlight year-round, making it the hottest zone. 2. Temperate Zones: Located between Tropics and Polar Circles (23.5° to 66.5° N/S). Sunlight falls at an angle, resulting in moderate temperatures and distinct seasons. 3. Frigid Zones: Located between Arctic/Antarctic Circles (66.5° N/S) and the Poles (90° N/S). Extremely cold due to slanting rays that barely rise above the horizon.

questions.question_text: Read the scenario: 'A international sports match starts in London (0° Greenwich) at 12:00 PM local time. Viewers in India want to watch it live.' At what IST time should Indian viewers tune in, and why?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. India's standard meridian is 82.5° E. 2. Time offset calculation: 82.5 × 4 minutes = 330 minutes = 5 hours and 30 minutes ahead of Greenwich Mean Time (GMT). 3. Therefore, when it is 12:00 PM in London, the live broadcast in India will be at 5:30 PM IST on the same day.

Why do we need a Standard Meridian for a country like India?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. India spans approximately 30° longitude from Gujarat in the west to Arunachal Pradesh in the east. 2. This longitude extent creates a local time difference of nearly 2 hours across the country. 3. A single Standard Meridian (82.5° E) ensures uniform timekeeping for railways, aviation, broadcasting, and administrative functions nationwide.

questions.question_text: What is the International Date Line and why does it curve at certain ocean locations?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. The International Date Line roughly follows the 180° meridian in the Pacific Ocean where the calendar date changes by one day. 2. It curves away from straight lines to avoid splitting island countries (like Kiribati) into two different calendar days.

questions.question_text: Describe the key components of a map and explain how conventional symbols facilitate map reading.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Distance (Scale): Converts real ground distances into proportional map measurements. 2. Direction: Uses cardinal (N, S, E, W) and intermediate points (NE, SE, SW, NW) oriented to North. 3. Symbols & Colors: Universal conventional signs (blue for water, brown for mountains, green for plains, icons for post offices/railways) allow anyone to read maps regardless of language barriers.

questions.question_text: Case Study: An explorer travels from 15° E longitude to 45° W longitude. Describe the time adjustment the explorer must make when setting their watch relative to Greenwich time.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. At 15° E: Time is 15 × 4 = 60 minutes (1 hour) ahead of Greenwich. 2. At 45° W: Time is 45 × 4 = 180 minutes (3 hours) behind Greenwich. 3. Total time difference between 15° E and 45° W = 1 hour + 3 hours = 4 hours behind the starting location.

Maps that show natural features such as mountains, plateaus, rivers, and oceans are called:
Compare physical maps and political maps.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Physical Maps show natural landforms and water bodies like rivers, plains, plateaus, and mountains using relief colors. 2. Political Maps display human-made boundaries, including cities, states, national borders, and capitals.

questions.question_text: Explain why the Torrid Zone receives the maximum amount of heat from the Sun.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. The Torrid Zone lies between the Tropic of Cancer (23.5°N) and Tropic of Capricorn (23.5°S). 2. At least once a year, the midday Sun is directly overhead at all latitudes in this zone. 3. Direct vertical rays concentrated on a smaller surface area deliver maximum solar radiation.

questions.question_text: Explain how longitude and Earth's rotation enable global timekeeping and standard time zones.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Earth rotates 360° on its axis in 24 hours, meaning it moves 15° every hour or 1° every 4 minutes. 2. Places east of Greenwich see the Sun earlier and are ahead in time, while places west are behind. 3. To prevent confusion from varying local times, countries adopt a central meridian (e.g., 82.5° E in India) as their Standard Time.

questions.question_text: Source-Based Analysis: Ancient astronomers like Varāhamihira and Āryabhaṭa studied meridians using Ujjain. Why was Ujjain chosen as the Madhya Rekhā in Indian astronomical texts?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Ujjain was located at the intersection of the Tropic of Cancer and a central north-south meridian line across India. 2. It was a renowned center for astronomical observatories and mathematical calculations. 3. Using Ujjain as a zero meridian provided a standardized reference point for regional calendar calculations (Pañchānga) before Greenwich was adopted globally.

State three advantages of a map over a globe.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Maps are flat, portable, and easy to carry or fold in books and atlases. 2. Maps can show detailed information about small areas (towns or districts) that cannot fit on a globe. 3. Maps can present specialized thematic themes like rainfall, roads, and land use.

questions.question_text: What is a compass and how does it assist navigators?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. A compass is a magnetic instrument used to determine directions. 2. Its magnetic needle always aligns pointing towards North-South. 3. Navigators use it to locate cardinal and intermediate directions at sea or on land.

questions.question_text: Describe the Frigid Zones and explain why they experience extreme cold and long periods of darkness.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. The Frigid Zones extend from 66.5° N/S (Arctic/Antarctic Circles) to the 90° N/S Poles. 2. The Sun's rays fall at extreme slanting angles in these polar regions, spreading warmth over vast areas. 3. Consequently, these zones experience severe cold, permanent ice, and seasonal phenomena like 24-hour daylight or darkness.

questions.question_text: Practical Exercise: A pilot flies directly east along the Equator from 0° Greenwich to 60° E longitude. How many time zones does the pilot cross, and what is the time difference?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Time difference per 15° longitude = 1 hour. 2. For 60° longitude change: 60 / 15 = 4 hours. 3. Since the flight is Eastward, local time at destination is 4 hours ahead of Greenwich time.

Explain the significance of the geographic grid system.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. The geographic grid is the network of intersecting latitudes and longitudes on a globe. 2. It allows precise pin-pointing of any location on Earth's surface using numerical coordinates (e.g., 28.6° N, 77.2° E for New Delhi). 3. It provides a standardized system for maritime, aerial, and satellite navigation (GPS).

questions.question_text: Why does GMT stand for Greenwich Mean Time and how is UTC related to it?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. GMT is named after the Prime Meridian passing through Greenwich, England. 2. It served as the original global reference for solar time calculation. 3. UTC (Coordinated Universal Time) is the modern high-precision atomic time standard based on GMT.

questions.question_text: Illustrate how a globe represents Earth's inclination (axis tilt) and discuss its impact on seasons.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. A globe's axis is tilted at an angle of 23.5° from the vertical line (or 66.5° to its orbital plane). 2. As Earth revolves around the Sun with this fixed tilt, different hemispheres lean towards or away from the Sun. 3. When the Northern Hemisphere tilts towards the Sun, it experiences summer with longer days, while the Southern Hemisphere experiences winter.

questions.question_text: Case Study: An Indian naval vessel at 82.5° E longitude communicates with a station in Japan at 135° E longitude. Calculate the local solar time difference between the vessel and the Japanese station.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Difference in longitudes = 135° - 82.5° = 52.5°. 2. Time difference = 52.5 × 4 minutes = 210 minutes = 3 hours and 30 minutes. 3. Since Japan is East of India, Japanese local time is 3 hours 30 minutes ahead of Indian time.
